title: SSDTrain: An Activation Offloading Framework to SSDs for Faster Large Language Model Training
problem: GPU memory capacity growth lags LLM size growth; activations (intermediate tensors from forward pass) dominate GPU memory use during training, limiting micro-batch size and increasing training overhead through expensive weight updates.
motivation: Training large LLMs requires offloading activations to reduce GPU memory pressure while maintaining training throughput through efficient I/O overlap.
method: SSDTrain adaptively offloads activations to high-capacity NVMe SSDs while fully overlapping data transfers with computation, employing tensor deduplication and forwarding optimizations, and integrating with PyTorch, Megatron, and DeepSpeed frameworks.
key_novelty: Adaptive activation offloading to NVMe SSDs with perfect I/O-computation overlap, enabling larger micro-batches and reduced training overhead without sacrificing throughput.
contributions: Adaptive activation offloading framework to NVMe SSDs
I/O-computation overlap techniques eliminating offloading overhead
Framework integration with PyTorch, Megatron, DeepSpeed
47% reduction in activation peak memory with negligible throughput loss
limitations: Not discussed; focus is on memory savings and throughput preservation.
primary_theme: Activation offloading to SSD for efficient LLM training
